transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. How can I help you today?

Um, hi. I guess… I’m here because I keep messing up basic life stuff. Like, I’ll forget to pay a bill, or I won’t reply to an interview email until it’s too late, or I’ll completely miss an appointment even if I meant to go. 

And then it turns into this whole thing where I’m trying to run errands and I’ll start one, get sidetracked, and somehow nothing actually gets done. It sounds small when I say it out loud, but it’s been costing me actual opportunities, and I’m kind of scared I’m not functioning like I’m supposed to.
Do you often find it hard to focus on tasks, even simple ones, and does this happen in different parts of your life, like work, home, or social situations?

Yeah, definitely. Like, I’ll sit down to do something simple-ish, like update my resume or work on a coding practice problem, and then my phone buzzes, or I hear someone talking outside, and suddenly I’m not doing it anymore. Or even just a random thought pops in, like, “Oh, I should check that other thing,” and I’m gone before I even realize I switched tasks.

It happens at home a lot, and with job stuff too. I’ll think I’m being productive, but then an hour passes and I’ve somehow done… not the thing I meant to do. It’s really frustrating because it’s not like I don’t care. I do care. My brain just gets pulled away so easily.
Do you often feel restless, fidgety, or as if you can't sit still for very long, especially when you're trying to focus on something?

Yeah, very much. Like if I’m in an interview or a meeting, or even just trying to watch a movie, I get this… pressure in my body, I guess? Like I need to shift around, stand up, tap something, mess with my hands—something—or I feel like I’m going to crawl out of my skin.

It’s weird because sometimes I’m trying really hard to look normal and still, especially in interviews, and then I’m thinking more about not moving than about what the person is saying. Even in movies, which are supposed to be relaxing, I’ll be changing positions or needing to get up for no real reason.
Looking back, were you noticeably distracted, impulsive, or restless as a child, or did you have trouble focusing on tasks or sitting still, especially in school or other structured settings?

Yeah, um… I think so. I mean, I don’t remember every detail, but I do remember elementary school comments being kind of the same over and over. Teachers would write that I was bright, which was nice, but then also that I lost worksheets constantly or didn’t follow directions because I’d rush through them.

And my desk was… honestly, like a disaster zone. I’d swear I had an assignment and then I’d be digging through crumpled papers and random stuff and couldn’t find it. I also got told I talked out of turn a lot. Like I’d have a thought and just say it, and then realize everyone was looking at me.

It’s funny, I can still picture those little report card comments—well, not funny, but you know what I mean. It was always “has potential” and then some note about being disorganized or too quick or interrupting.
Have these symptoms of distraction, restlessness, and difficulty getting things done caused you noticeable problems in your relationships, work, or other important areas of life?

Yeah… it’s definitely caused problems. Since I got fired, it’s like all the little steps you’re supposed to do to get back on track just keep falling apart. Like interview follow-ups—I’ll fully mean to send them, and then somehow I miss the window, or I remember at some random time when I’m in the shower or making coffee, and then later it’s gone again.

And I had this volunteer project I actually cared about, which is embarrassing because it wasn’t even like I didn’t want to do it. I did. But I couldn’t keep up with the basic organizing and follow-through, so I had to step back from it.

So now I’m unemployed, and I feel like I can’t reliably manage the basic stuff to move my life forward. Like the steps are not hard individually, but putting them together and actually doing them when they need to happen… I keep messing that up.
